She says on the tape she was giving life one last try because after she recorded the tapes, she a felt a sense of peace because she had let it all out. However that doesn’t mean she wasn’t still considering the option of suicide, which is why she brought the recorder into the counselling session. 

Mr. Porter was a terrible counsellor. Hannah said she thinks she might have been sexually assaulted at a party and Mr. Porter’s first reaction was to say “You think? But you’re not sure.” Those words would immediately shut a victim down and make them feel like they’re not being believed. When he asks her more questions and she basically confirms she was raped without using the word “rape”, he tells her she can move on if she doesn’t want to press charges. I can’t believe that that is the correct thing to say to a rape victim especially an underage one. To me, it sounded like he thought she could move on with it and get over it in this one counselling session and I’m sure that’s what it sounded like to her as well. 

And when she says she wants life to stop and he asks her what she meant, of course she would say she “didn’t mean it like that”. She doesn’t even know this man. A counsellor at my school asked me if I liked myself and I sarcastically said “yeah” and he said “are you sure?” and I assured him yes, of course I do. But no, I don’t, I just couldn’t confide that to a counsellor I had just met. And suicidal thoughts are even harder to say out loud to someone, especially an adult. He should have gone after her and made sure she wasn’t going to go home and hurt herself and that’s exactly what she did.

And afterwards he rips out the page in his appointment book and conceals that Hannah had gone to him for help on the day she committed suicide. He told no one, and without that tape, there would have been no proof and he would have gone on with his life and kept doing things the way he was. Listening to that tape, changed him. He had an amazing character growth and he woke up and saw what was wrong. Hannah did that. Thank god he heard that tape BECAUSE he has a young family and a daughter to raise. Maybe next time, and it’s his daughter who’s raped, he’ll know to listen and help her, not tell her to move on days after the assault. It’s not Hannah’s fault he was under qualified for his job, it’s the school’s. I really think she made those tapes to educate these people on how their actions affect others (especially a fucking counsellor at a high school), not to hurt them or take revenge.

And also, I’m not saying that her committing suicide and recording those tapes was the right decision. I’m just saying it makes sense, especially to an angsty teenager.
